title: Voyager: The Machines That Refused to Die

scenes.text: In November 2023, the most distant machine humans ever built started speaking nonsense. Twenty-four billion kilometres away, Voyager 1 was dying, and nobody on Earth knew why.
Every message took twenty-two hours to reach it. Every answer took twenty-two more. The engineers who designed it had mostly retired. Some had died.
What a handful of people did next is one of the greatest repair jobs in history. But to understand it, we have to go back to 1977.
In the summer of 1977, the outer planets lined up in a way that happens once every hundred and seventy-five years.
One spacecraft could swing from Jupiter to Saturn to Uranus to Neptune, stealing speed from each.
NASA built two of them, and bolted a golden record to each, just in case someone out there was listening.
Today both Voyagers are still running, on less power than a toaster, with computers weaker than a car key.
And every day, a radio dish somewhere on Earth still listens for them. Follow for the full story of how they were saved.
